title: fix(scripts): check-side-effects-array walks every published entry point, not just the source barrel
body:
Fixes #8850

`check-side-effects-array` derived its enumeration from **one** graph: the single `src/index.*` that `deriveSpellingMap` round-trips on. `manifestEntryForms` already collected every form the manifest publishes, but only the barrel anchored the walk and only the barrel anchored `checkReachability`. A registrar reachable only from a secondary entry was therefore invisible — never proposed as MISSING, and, if the array named it anyway, reported STALE. That second half is why this was p2 and not a coverage nit: the gate did not merely miss the defect, it **argued for introducing one**.

## The population, re-derived — and what the PR has to say plainly

Triage asked for the multi-entry population to be established first. Re-derived in this worktree over **46** workspace manifests, using the gate's own subpath rule rather than the gate's reader:

| package declaring an array | forms published | what the second form is |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `@object-ui/app-shell` | `dist/index.js` · `src/styles.css` | a **CSS asset** — not a module a graph walk can traverse |
| `@object-ui/layout` | `dist/index.js` · `dist/index.umd.cjs` | the `require` half of the **same** subpath `.` — a second **format** |

Two array-declaring packages, both "multi-entry" by form count, and **neither has a second entry point with its own source module**. ⇒ **the genuine multi-entry population is zero today.** The fix is still right, but the priority claim rests on **future** packages, not present ones. Empirically: with the widened walk ablated back to a single root, this repo's gate still exits 0 with identical output — no verdict in this workspace changes.

The card's *"`@object-ui/app-shell` publishes 31 entries"* is a misread: **31 is the length of its `sideEffects` array**; the manifest publishes **2** forms. The walk-cost concern in question 2 has no present instance behind it. It is answered anyway (below), because it will have one.

`@object-ui/types` publishes 12 export entries including `./zod`, whose barrel genuinely is unreachable from `src/index.ts` — that is the card's real demonstration. It declares `sideEffects: false`, so `readArrayPackages` excludes it: it **proves** the defect and **cannot** be the fixture that pins it. Hence a synthetic fixture, built deliberately.

## What changed

**The walk roots at every entry POINT**, in one traversal over a shared `seen` set (card question 2: N entries cost the *union* of their graphs, never N times one graph). **Reachability widened with it** (question 3): a registrar is retained when **any** entry reaches it through covered modules.

**Which forms are entry points is derived, not listed** (question 1). `exports` keys starting with `.` are **subpaths** — separate things a consumer imports, so separate graph roots. Everything *below* a subpath is a condition or a fallback array, and those choose a build **format** of the same entry. `classifyEntryForms` sorts every published form on that structure plus what is on disk:

- **`entry-point`** — the inverse of the spelling map lands on a source module that exists. Walked.
- **`duplicate-entry`** — an alias subpath resolving to a source module another subpath already claimed. Same root, no new modules.
- **`alternate-format`** — the form did not invert, but a form under the **same subpath** did. `layout`'s `.cjs` reaches exactly what its `.js` reaches.
- **`asset`** — the form names a file present in the package exactly as published and not a module this gate reads. A stylesheet is a resolution target, not a graph root: there is no import to follow out of it. Positive on both halves (the file is *there*, and no source module produces it), never "the map returned undefined".

### Why the loud case is "cannot CLASSIFY", not "cannot map"

The card asked for the inverse of `toPublished` to *"fail loudly when it cannot"* map a form. Taken literally that turns the gate **red on both of its current packages on day one**: a stylesheet and a duplicate format are exactly the two shapes the inverse cannot map, and neither is a defect. So the distinction drawn is between a form that **is a second entry point** and one that **provably is not a new graph root** — and the loud case is a form that is *neither*, positively classified as neither. A form silently skipped is a graph **root** silently skipped, and a registrar behind it would never be proposed as MISSING: that is this gate's own silent-drop failure class rebuilt one level up.

No extension allow-list and no package name is tested anywhere in the classification.

One guard was **removed** rather than added: a proposed inverse round-trip assertion on the barrel could not be made to fail — `sourceBarrel` is discovered by the same extension order `toSource` searches, so the two agree by construction. A guard that cannot fire is not protection. The hazard it would have covered is covered by a check that *can* fire: an inverse that stops landing on source modules makes the barrel's own subpath unclassifiable, and the gate exits 2. The comment says so in place of the guard.

## The fixture and its ablation

Since the real population is zero, the fixture is the only evidence the fix works. A synthetic package with two subpaths whose registrar sits behind the second one, plus partners for the format / asset / alias / unclassifiable shapes.

Ablation — the union of roots reverted to the pre-change single root, on a committed tree, mutation proven on disk by grep counts and by a `git hash-object` differing from the `HEAD` blob:

| leg | result |
|:--|:--|
| **red** (barrel-only walk) | **6 failed** / 38 passed. The registrar is not proposed as MISSING, and the honest array reads `stale: ["dist/registrar.js", "src/registrar.ts", "src/secondary.ts"]` — the gate telling the author to delete a live registration, which is the p2 consequence reproduced. |
| **green** (restored) | **44 passed**, `git diff HEAD` empty, restored blob `d8e18800` byte-identical to the `HEAD` blob. |
| real workspace, both legs | exit 0, identical output — the "population is zero today" sentence, measured. |

## Gates run

| gate | printed verdict |
|:--|:--|
| `check-side-effects-array.mjs` | exit 0 — both packages green, `449` / `8` modules walked from 1 entry point each |
| `scripts/__tests__` (full, behind the shared verify lock) | `139 passed \| 2 skipped (141)`, `4152 passed \| 2 skipped`, wrapper `VERDICT command-exit 0` |
| `type-check:scripts` | exit 0 |
| `lint:root` (whole root population, not narrowed) | exit 0 — 318 files, 0 errors, 32 pre-existing warnings; the two changed files 0/0 |
| `check-new-cross-file-line-citations.mjs` | `VERDICT ... 0 new citation(s) -> exit 0` |
| `check-control-bytes.mjs` | exit 0 — 7277 tracked text files scanned |
| `check-changeset-presence.mjs` | exit 0 — *"No source or published contract of a released package changed in this range, so no changeset is owed"* (2 files changed, 0 published source, 0 manifest contract moved) ⇒ **no changeset added** |
| `check-sdui-registration-pins.mjs` | exit 2 **PREREQUISITE NOT MET** — *"No console build to weigh"*; unrelated to this diff (it needs a built console). Its fixture suite passes, and it consumes only `map.error` / `map.srcRoot`, both unchanged. Declared to CI. |

## Not done

The gate's `--list` output now reports each subpath's classification, which is new surface for a reader but changes no verdict. Nothing else in the repo was touched; no package's `sideEffects` declaration was changed, and no threshold, assertion or pin was lowered.
